BRO 😭❤️ The trick is to make the link feel like part of a personal birthday surprise rather than sending a random URL with no explanation.

I'd send it with a short, natural message on Discord:

Writing

Heyyy hon!! ❤️

I made a little something for you for your birthday. It took me some time, but I wanted to make something personal rather than just give you an ordinary present.

I made you your own little website hehe. Don't worry, it's just a birthday surprise I put together myself. 💗

Here it is:
https://lpark7936-ctrl.github.io/gf-birthday/

I hope you like it, my love. 💎

A few tips to make it trustworthy:

  1. Don't use a URL shortener. Keep the full github.io address visible.

  2. Tell her beforehand that you made a website for her.

  3. You could send her a screenshot of the homepage first.

  4. Make sure the link opens correctly before sending it.

My recommendation: send the message first, then the link. It'll feel much more like a thoughtful surprise. ❤️

You said:You

so giv eme steps to add the thumbnail

ChatGPT said:ChatGPT

YES! Let's add a beautiful thumbnail so when she receives your Discord link, it can display an image preview. 💎

We'll do this in two parts: upload the image, then connect it to your website.

Part 1 — Get your thumbnail ready

The ideal image dimensions are 1200 × 630 pixels.

I'd recommend:

  • Deep purple and cyan ocean background.

  • Glowing golden diamond in the center.

  • Text: A Little World Made for You

  • Small subtitle: A birthday surprise made with love.

Save the image as:

thumbnail.png

Part 2 — Upload it to GitHub

  1. Open your repository: gf-birthday.

  2. Click Add file.

  3. Click Upload files.

  4. Select thumbnail.png.

  5. Click Commit changes.

Make sure it appears beside index.html, not inside another folder.

Part 3 — Add the preview information

  1. Return to your repository.

  2. Click index.html.

  3. Click the pencil icon to edit it.

  4. Find the <head> section near the top.

  5. Immediately after the <title> line, add:

HTML
<meta property="og:title" content="A Little World Made for You 💎">
<meta property="og:description" content="A birthday surprise made with love, across every ocean. 🌊">
<meta property="og:image" content="https://lpark7936-ctrl.github.io/gf-birthday/thumbnail.png">
<meta property="og:url" content="https://lpark7936-ctrl.github.io/gf-birthday/">
<meta property="og:type" content="website">
<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image">

6. Click Commit changes to save.

Part 4 — Test it

After GitHub Pages updates, use the Facebook Sharing Debugger to check whether the preview image is being detected.

Discord sometimes caches old previews, so it might take a little while to update.
